title: Living research dossier
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for keeping a research dossier current: a numbered queue of open questions worked in cycles, with at most one sub-agent per question in each cycle; sourced answers folded in and a cycle log appended; every fact carrying an as-of date and a decay class; a switch to watching named triggers once the questions run out; decayed facts refreshed against their sources; and a person deciding which version is published. It pins the deep research report pack's questions, source logs, claims and reviews instead of redefining them.
boundaries: Permitted access only, as the deep research report pack's rules say: official APIs, feeds and pages, robots.txt and terms respected, no logins, paywall bypasses or personal data.
At most one sub-agent per question in a cycle; every sub-agent is named in the cycle log.
No scheduler is activated: every cycle, trigger check and refresh is a verb an authorized requester enqueues.
Only a person decides which dossier version is published.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for keeping a research dossier current

value.lets_workers: Keep a dossier on a topic people keep relying on: number its open questions and work them in cycles, with at most one sub-agent per question in each cycle; fold sourced answers in and append a cycle log; give every fact an as-of date, a decay class and a refresh date; switch to watching named triggers once no question is open; refresh facts as they decay; and leave the decision about which version is published to a person. Questions, source logs, claims and reviews use the deep research report pack's nouns.
value.not_for: A question answered once. One cited answer is a deep research report; a dossier is for a topic whose answers go stale.

flow.when: A topic that must stay current gets a numbered queue.
Each cycle picks open questions, one sub-agent each.
The one sub-agent for one question in one cycle.
Sourced answers, refreshes and fired triggers make a new version.
Every cycle appends what changed and who worked what.
No question is open: name the triggers.
Each check of the named triggers, as the requester enqueues it.
Facts past their refresh date are read again.
Before anyone relies on a version; a different worker.
A person decides which version is published.

value.worked_example: Synthetic: a dossier on cold-storage grants for small food banks. Two cycles answer three questions and park one; the dossier switches to watching three triggers; a volatile closing date is refreshed; a changed guidelines page fires a trigger that reopens two questions; a third cycle supersedes the award range and parks the fiscal sponsor question again; a person decides the version that is published.

relations: A dossier is a deep research report kept current.

nouns.title: How a dossier is opened, worked in cycles, watched and refreshed
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: open-dossier writes the first version: the topic, a numbered question queue and the role of the person who decides what is published.
plan-cycle picks open questions in number order up to the cycle's limit and proposes one answer-question verb for each; nobody else works those questions in that cycle.
answer-question, the sub-agent, answers one question with a source log and a claim extract in the deep research report pack's shapes.
fold-in writes the next version by compare-and-set; log-cycle appends the cycle log.
When no question is open, switch-to-watching names the triggers; check-triggers and refresh-decayed-facts run whenever the requester enqueues them, and fold-in applies what they find.
review-dossier, by a worker that wrote none of it, comes before a person decides a version is published.
rules: The dossier is one noun with versions; only fold-in and switch-to-watching write it, each by compare-and-set against the version it read.
Answers, cycle logs, trigger checks and refresh records are written once and never edited.
A sub-agent reads the dossier version its cycle plan pins, so answers in one cycle never see each other.
An answer whose facts lack exact quotes from sources read through permitted access is not folded in.
A fired trigger sends the dossier back to working questions; watching resumes when the queue runs out again.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue. A person decides which version is published.

nouns.title: Guardrail: at most one sub-agent per question in a cycle
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: In one cycle, at most one sub-agent works any one question. A question that needs more work waits for the next cycle, and every sub-agent is named in the cycle log beside the question it worked.
value.how_it_is_checked: Each cycle plan and cycle log lists a question at most once, and the dossier's fan-out summary never exceeds one.

nouns.title: Guardrail: every fact has an as-of date and a decay class
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every fact carries its as-of date, the day it was last confirmed against its source, a decay class and the refresh date that follows from them. A fact past its refresh date is due until it is read again, and is never shown as current.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every fact has as_of, decay_class and refresh_by; refresh_by follows from the decay classes; and a dossier anyone relies on lists nothing as due.

nouns.title: Guardrail: nothing in a dossier is overwritten
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A changed fact keeps its earlier statement, as-of date and sources, marked superseded by the fact that replaced it, and every cycle appends a log, so a reader can see what the dossier said on any date and why it changed.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every superseded fact names its replacement and the reason, and every cycle the dossier lists names its log.

nouns.title: The numbered question queue
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same queue and answers always give the same result.

rules: Number questions 1, 2, 3 in the order they are added, and never reuse or renumber one.
Each question is one a source could answer, framed like the deep research report pack's research question: its scope, definitions and what would change the answer.
Status is open, partial, answered, parked, split or duplicate. No question is deleted: split names its new numbers and duplicate names the question it repeats.
Park a question, with the reason and what would reopen it, when the permitted sources cannot answer it or after three cycles without an answer.
An answer that raises a new question adds it after the last number, saying which cycle and question raised it.
open_questions counts open and partial questions; the queue has run out when it is zero.

nouns.title: Working the queue in cycles
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same plan and answers always give the same log.

rules: A cycle is plan, answer, fold in and log, numbered one after the last.
plan-cycle picks open and partial questions lowest number first, up to max_questions (three by default), and lists every open question it did not pick with the reason.
One answer-question verb is proposed per picked question; a second sub-agent on the same question waits for the next cycle.
A cycle stops at its time budget; unfinished questions stay open.
A cycle that folds nothing in still appends a log that says why.
Each sub-agent's task id, model and cost belong in its own execution report; a cost nobody measured stays null with a reason.

nouns.title: Decay classes: how long a fact stays current
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same fact, class and date always give the same refresh date.

stable.for: definitions in a dated text, past events, a published study's reported result

slow.for: laws and rules in force, eligibility that changes yearly, an organization's structure

periodic.for: award sizes, quarterly or annual figures, budgets, published schedules

fast.for: prices, software versions, contacts by role, rules under revision

volatile.for: open calls, deadlines within the month, counts that change daily

rules: refresh_by is as_of plus the class's days; when the source states an earlier end, such as a deadline, refresh_by is that date.
Choose the fastest class that fits; between two, take the faster.
A fact is due when its refresh_by is before the check date.
A refreshed fact that still holds gets a new as_of and refresh_by; one that changed is superseded by a new fact.
A source that cannot be read leaves the fact due, never confirmed.

nouns.title: Named triggers: watching for changes once the questions run out
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same source state always gives the same result.

rules: Watching starts only when no question is open or partial.
Every trigger has a name, the one source it watches, how it is checked, what change fires it and the questions it reopens; every question with a fact that is not stable has at least one.
Check cheaply: a conditional request with the validator the source last returned, a feed's newest entry id, the SHA-256 of one named section's text, or a date passing.
Unchanged is not fired. A change fires only when it matches the trigger's condition; other changes are noted as changed_not_fired.
A source that fails two checks in a row is unreachable, not fired, and the facts it supports become due.
A fired trigger reopens its questions and the dossier goes back to working them in cycles.
Triggers watch public sources through permitted access only, never a person or a page behind a login.
A cadence is a suggestion to the requester. No scheduler is activated; each check is a verb an authorized requester enqueues.

nouns.category_reason: A deterministic check suite with known-good and known-bad examples; the validator recomputes every verdict.

verbs.title: Open a dossier with a numbered question queue
verbs.summary: Turn a topic people will keep relying on into a first dossier version: its scope, a numbered queue of questions a source could answer, and the role of the person who decides what is published.
verbs.outcome: A dossier in questions mode, or no_change with a pointer when one cited answer is enough.

steps: Write three to seven opening questions numbered from 1, each one a source could answer, framed like the research question template.
Carry a fact over from earlier work only with its claims, sources, as-of date and decay class; anything else becomes a question.
Name the role of the person who decides what is published, never a person.
End no_change when the request needs one answer once, and propose the deep research report pack's frame-question verb.

verbs.summary: Pick the open questions this cycle works, lowest number first up to the cycle's limit, and propose exactly one answer-question verb for each picked question.
verbs.outcome: A cycle plan with its proposed answer-question verbs, or no_change when no question is open.

steps: Verify the pin, and number the cycle one after the dossier's last.

Propose one answer-question verb per picked question, pinned to this dossier version, and none for a question another sub-agent already holds this cycle.
End no_change when no question is open or partial, and propose switch-to-watching.

No question appears twice in picked, and proposed_verbs holds exactly one answer-question verb per picked question.

verbs.outcome: A new dossier version by compare-and-set, or no_change when nothing passes the fold-in rules.

verbs.title: Decide whether a dossier version is published (a person)
verbs.summary: A person reads one dossier version and its review and decides whether that exact version is delivered to its readers, or held with the reason, such as a fact still due or a dispute to settle first.
verbs.outcome: A delivery record for one dossier version.

slots.name: dossier
slots.description: Pin of the exact dossier version.

slots.name: review
slots.description: Pin of the review of that version.

steps: Run both checklists.
Deliver only a version whose review passed and whose dossier checks pass; holding is a valid decision, with the reason.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.delivery-record's schema.
A deliver decision has review_passed true, and output_ref names the exact dossier version.
The submitting key belongs to a person who neither wrote nor reviewed the dossier.
